scope: Independent original-detail review of four modern kingdom application illustrations
globalConditions: Fictional present-day reflective applications; no visible Christ and no claim of documentary or literal scriptural depiction.
Technical review is not owner approval, browser verification or import evidence.

entries.alt: A gardener lowers a seed into a soil-filled planting tray while other gardeners work behind her.
entries.caption: A gardener gives a seed a place to grow. This imagined present-day scene invites reflection on Jesus' mustard-seed comparison and the significance of small beginnings.
entries.findings: Seed pinched at fingertips above tray; hand anatomy, contact and attentive downward gaze are plausible. Natural face and materials. Seed is relatively large and not identifiable as mustard.
conditions: Do not call the visible seed a mustard seed or present this modern scene as a literal reconstruction of the parable.
No guaranteed harvest or promised outcome.

entries.alt: A man presses and folds dough with both hands on a floured kitchen worktop.
entries.caption: A baker works dough in a modern kitchen. This imagined scene recalls the familiar process Jesus draws on in His comparison of the kingdom to leaven.
entries.findings: Both hands contact and compress the dough credibly; visible fingers and wrists are coherent. Natural face, focused gaze and photographic kitchen detail. A proofing pan supports bread-making context, but yeast itself and rising over time are not visible.
conditions: Describe kneading, not a visible insertion of leaven or a verified time-lapse transformation.
Keep the connection reflective; this modern male baker is not the woman specified in the parable.

entries.alt: A woman sets a phone on a shelf while exchanging an attentive look with a man seated beside an open book.
entries.caption: Two adults give a learning conversation their attention as a phone is set aside. This imagined application of the pearl comparison invites reflection on how our choices of time express what we consider precious.
entries.findings: Reciprocal gaze, phone placement and pointing hand on book are coherent. Both adults participate with natural dignity; no infantilizing treatment. No legible private phone content.
conditions: Do not claim a promised hour elapsed, verified literacy level, nationality or learning outcome.
Tutoring is a fictional scenario premise rather than a biography established by appearance.

entries.alt: One young person places a cardboard display on a shelf while two others arrange patterned fabric at a worktable.
entries.caption: The group makes room for a fabric project while keeping a handmade display nearby. This imagined application invites reflection on what we choose to make room for when we recognize something valuable.
entries.findings: Display supported by visible hand and shelf; other arm partly occluded plausibly. Fabric handling and hands are coherent; cutting tool rests unused on a mat. Task-directed eyes and natural agency, photographic detail.
conditions: Do not claim a completed donation project or identify recipients not shown.
Avoid treating artwork or display-making as inherently worthless; the visible action supports rearranging priorities, not contempt for creativity.
